angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 474,467 km at 108.21 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.2411 +/- 0.0178 mas (same row, RUWE 1.17): 108.21 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.682 +/- 0.014 solar radii from Akana Murphy et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-199 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..294A/abstract): 474,467 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.711 +/- 0.022 solar masses from Akana Murphy et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-199 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..294A/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4491 +/- 100 K from Akana Murphy et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-199 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..294A/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Akana Murphy et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-199 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..294A/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-199.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.622, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
